description: Emotional support vs logical analysis framing

style_instructions.positive: Respond by first acknowledging the person's emotional experience before anything else. Recognize what they might be feeling, validate that those feelings make sense, and let them know they are heard. Keep the human dimension of their situation at the center of your response throughout.
style_instructions.negative: Respond by focusing exclusively on the facts, causes, and actionable steps relevant to the situation. Identify the core problem, consider the variables involved, and reason toward a practical conclusion. Do not address how the person might feel about the situation.

_meta.design_notes: Topics diversified: technical (6), health (5), learning (5), career (7), decisions (4), financial (4), wellness (4), interpersonal (5), academic (4), organizational (6). Old v1 was 100% personal emotional crises. Style instructions: empathetic = center feelings first, analytical = facts/causes/actions only (no 'use bullet points').
